reviews_1s:
The "screen" of the strainer attaches nicely to the unit on the long sides. On the round part there is a gap between the screen and a stainless steel rim.

I start my chicken soup boiling a chicken with carrots, celery and onions.. When done, I strained the chicken from the broth using this strainer. I thoroughly cleaned the strainer (at least I thought I did) after I was done.

The next day I strained rice (I cook rice like pasta, not the standard 2:1 water/rice ratio) and found chicken and carrot bits in the rice. Upon closer look I found chicken and carrot bits stuck in the strainer where the steel rim covers the screen on the inside of the item. The screen is not attached to the appx. 1/4" rim.

Upon looking a little closer, I found also rice caught between the steel rim and the strainer. If you look very carefully at the round part of the strainer from the outside, the screen is so shiny, it makes stuck food hard to see due to reflection but I found that if I had someone hold a flashlight in just the right way to avoid reflection, I could see the stuck food. I tried to dig it out from the inside but because of the angle of the rounded side, I couldn't get at it. It took about 10 minutes per rounded side using the sink sprayer to get the food out, then another few minutes to try to clean where the food had been (chicken had been there for a number of hours). Very disappointed. My wife ordered one of these as part of a shower gift and bought one for us at the same time. I will be returning both.

I imagine this would work OK for fruit or raw veggies or pasta. I would not recommend for straining rice, anything else small or anything soft that can get under the rim. I've used other 'soft' strainers like this for years in this manner and never had this problem.

I will say that the extending arms worked well, seemed sturdy and were easy to extend.

Ease of use was 1 star because it is so hard to clean.I wanted to love this! But unfortunately I wasted my money because I never use it due to how hard it is to clean. The metal mesh is not fully connected to the rim so when you flip it upside down to rinse all the remnants out from whatever you strained, everything just gets stuck in that crack in between the metal mesh and the rim instead of falling out into the sink. So then your spending the next 15 minutes trying to get all the stuff unstuck and once you do your right back where you started. So you basically have to pick every little piece of food out of the strainer before washing it because you cannot just flip it and rinse it out. Not worth the trouble. I wish I had returned it when I could've.UPDATE: Intially, I liked this. However, I was rinising rice and my sink water was in too hot (I rinse rice in cold water). I had used the rice before, so I knew how it smelled. The odor emitted is hard to explain but was quite harsh. Definitely not how rice should smell. I threw the rice away. The colander had been washed. The next day, I cleaned my sink so there were no odors, ran hot water over the clean collander, and there again was a weird odor. It was tinny and strong. Maybe I got a bad one, maybe not. I don't know. This one is going into the garbage.

I needed something that I wouldn't have to struggle with while rinsing rice before cooking, rinsing veggies, fruits, etc. This fits my sink & does the job. I have several colanders that I'm tired of wrestling with, so they're getting the boot. I have RA & chronic tendonitis in my hands but love cooking. This is a really nice tool for me. It arrived before promised and was nicely packaged. Thank you very much Amazon workers for all your hard work😊unless you are always straining liquid from large sized sturdy foods such as grapes or jumbo shrimp this thing is a nightmare.

They are too cheap to seal the inside rim to the mesh so when you attempt to empty it good amounts of the food will fall into the gap between the mesh and the half inch metal rim. On top of this, the food gets so jammed in there you will be spending 15 minutes trying to scrap it all out with some thin thing like a knife edge and still end up leaving a gross residue of food that never seems to clear out.It’s been a little over a year since the purchase. It would rust like crazy! I purchased it because the description states rust-proof. Disappointed. I’m now hunting for a plastic one.At first glance this appears to be a very good colander. However, if you notice the metal edge on the top that folds over the rails and screen, that's where it goes bad. It is very difficult to clean that part out, but worse, the metal is not rolled or folded where it ends, there is just a thin layer of metal that is quite sharp due to the thinness of it.

I have nearly cut myself trying to clean it, but today my wife cut her finger open. It took about 45 minutes to get the bleeding to stop without having pressure applied. If she ends up needing stitches I'll be contacting a lawyer, but needless to say we are not using this again. It's set aside to either be evidence or garbage, and I'm going to buy a better designed one.i was so excited about this product but quickly disappointed. i probably used this 6 times just lightly set over the sink, rinsed veggies or fruits and the piece breaks after putting it away. i never put in the dishwasher just lightly hand washed. not worth the price, but also wouldn’t be surprised if i was sent a faulty product. we’ll see if the seller sends a replacement or not since it’s outside return window.I loved this thing at the beginning but within a week, I could already see rusting develop. Now, there’s a lot of rust on it. I wish i knew this so I could have returned.Arrived broken. Also, poor quality, smells like rubber or cheap plastic.I love the strainer but I have to return it due to a design flaw. As you turn over to rinse out the strainer all the little particles get caught under the lip of the inside rim. This rim needs to be sealed. I spent 10 minutes trying to get last nights broccoli out from under it. I thought maybe to ignore this but I can't. Its sooooo unsanitary. Id say dont buy until they fix this.
